clue.text: Invents the ideal drink

parts.note: the ideal thing is a dream, as in 'a dream home'
to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Someone concocts the perfect cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream up a scheme is to devise or concoct it from imagination.

clue.text: Agent put down for the second showing

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
to lay something is to put it down

explanation.surface: A theatrical agent is dropped before a show is repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: A replay is a match or broadcast shown or played again.

clue.text: Judicial decision causing conflict in our times

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other here

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels the years of the present era
a war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A court ruling sparks modern-day strife.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a sum or ruling granted by a court or arbitrator after judgment.

clue.text: Angry because condensation has fallen

explanation.surface: Someone is cross because their windows are fogged.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamed up is slang for furious, and literally describes glass misted over with water droplets.

clue.text: Prosperous artist in Syria

parts.note: palmy days are flourishing, prosperous ones
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A wealthy painter is living in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an ancient desert city, now ruins, in central Syria.

clue.text: Local worker in the legal profession

explanation.surface: A pub employee who also practises law.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub (a 'local' in Britain) is staffed by bar staff; a barrister belongs to the Bar, the legal profession.

clue.text: Perk for ex-student backed by his union

indicators.note: backed tells us the ex-student's letters are written backwards

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil
the NUS is the National Union of Students, a student's union

explanation.surface: A graduate gets a benefit backed by their students' union.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an extra payment or advantage, a perk on top of pay.

clue.text: Bertrand resolved to keep many of his paintings

indicators.note: to keep means the rearranged name holds another letter within it
resolved, in the sense of broken down and recast, tells us to rearrange Bertrand

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: Bertrand decides to hold on to several of an artist's pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges BERTRAND into REBRANDT, and 'to keep' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's name stands for his works, as in 'the gallery owns a Rembrandt'.

clue.text: Channels used to get Cockney a perm?

indicators.note: London Cockney speech drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: a perm puts curls, or waves, into hair

explanation.surface: A hairdressing query: is broadcasting how a Londoner gets curls?
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys famously drop their aitches, so HAIR WAVES loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: The airwaves are the radio frequencies used by broadcast channels.

clue.text: Drug a poet I maltreated

indicators.note: maltreated suggests the words are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to drugging and abusing a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium-derived narcotics such as morphine are classed together under this name.

clue.text: Watershed for German state and German currency

parts.note: a Land is one of the federal states of Germany
the mark was Germany's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: A turning point for Germany's politics and money.
explanation.definitionFit: A watershed moment is a turning point, a milestone in history.

clue.text: My Arnold converted without premeditation

indicators.note: converted means the letters are changed into another form

explanation.surface: Arnold converted on impulse, without forethought.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something haphazardly, by chance, is acting with no forethought.

clue.text: Pate? There's a feast!

explanation.surface: Someone serving a pâté at a lavish table.
explanation.definitionFit: Pâté is something spread on toast, and a lavish meal laid out on a table is also called this.

clue.text: What the amorous loan shark did?

definitions.text: What the amorous loan shark did?

parts.words: What the amorous loan shark did?
parts.note: a romantic suitor makes passes, while a moneylender lends money up front: one phrase covers both

explanation.surface: A moneylender falls in love and courts someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Making sexual approaches and lending sums of money in advance are both described by this phrase.

clue.text: Diana's light, illicit liquor

explanation.surface: Bootleg spirits glow under the goddess's light.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana is the Roman moon goddess, so her glow is lunar light; illegally distilled whisky is also called this.

clue.text: Force five English macho males to go to church

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
he-men are muscular, macho men
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Five tough English guys are made to attend a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehemence is forceful intensity of feeling or expression.

clue.text: Become reconciled to court

parts.note: to make up after a quarrel is to become friends again
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two parties settle their differences before going to law.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up to someone is to flatter or woo them, to court their favour.

clue.text: PM supporting man in training. Isaiah, perhaps

parts.note: John Major was a British Prime Minister
pro means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: PT is physical training
he is a pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister backs a man in training, Isaiah perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaiah is one of the four longer prophetic books of the Old Testament, alongside Jeremiah, Ezekiel and Daniel.

clue.text: Counterpart writes poetic epitaph

parts.note: OB, for obiit ('died'), is carved on gravestones
to verse is to write poetry

explanation.surface: A fellow poet composes lines for a tombstone.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse is the matching opposite side of a coin or argument, its counterpart.

clue.text: Physician and I are from old Florentine family

parts.note: a medic is a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor and I are descended from Renaissance Italian nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: The rulers and bankers of Renaissance Florence bore this surname.

clue.text: Landlord gets comparatively little otherwise

parts.note: less is the comparative of little
or introduces an alternative, otherwise

explanation.surface: A landlord gets less money than you might expect.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessor is one who grants a lease, the property owner renting it out.

clue.text: Irritable because of rodent infestation

explanation.surface: Someone is cross because their house has rats.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British slang for bad-tempered, and literally means overrun by rats.

clue.text: Bloodsuckers fill seductive women with rage

indicators.note: fill means the second piece goes into the middle of the first

parts.note: vamps are seductive femmes fatales
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Leeches make femmes fatales furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Legendary undead creatures that drink human blood are bloodsuckers.

clue.text: Some kindling left by the fireplace

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some wood for a fire is left next to the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: An inglenook is a corner by a hearth; the word on its own means the fire or fireside.

clue.text: He runs a small typesetting machine

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels
a printer is a machine that sets out type

explanation.surface: A man operates a compact printing press.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner of short races is a sprinter.

clue.text: Little mug containing egg-flip and spirit

parts.note: egg-flip is another name for eggnog, or nog
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A small cup holding eggnog and gin.
explanation.definitionFit: A noggin is a small cup or mug, or a small measure of drink.

clue.text: Manage to obtain pass

explanation.surface: Someone gets hold of something and walks past.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire something is to come by it; to come by is also to drop in or pass someone's way.

clue.text: It explains why six geese went astray

indicators.note: went astray says the letters have wandered out of order

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about wandering geese.
explanation.definitionFit: Exegesis is critical explanation or interpretation, especially of scripture.
